title: The God of Small Things

vibeProfile.oneLine: A forbidden love across caste sets off a family tragedy in Kerala.

summary: In a lush corner of Kerala, twins Rahel and Estha grow up amid a family's secrets, and a single forbidden act of love across caste lines sets off a tragedy whose consequences ripple across decades. Arundhati Roy's Booker-winning debut tells its story in shimmering, inventive, non-linear prose, circling the wound at its heart. Sensuous, heartbreaking and politically fierce about caste and desire, it is one of the most acclaimed Indian novels ever written and a landmark of contemporary fiction.
whyReadIt: Roy's Booker-winning debut, a Kerala family tragedy told in shimmering, inventive prose. Sensuous and heartbreaking.

funFacts.text: It won the Booker Prize in 1997 and was Roy's first novel.
